topic: The day a week you lose to paperwork
objective: Show a contractor that the admin time they treat as unavoidable is a system problem, not a discipline problem.
hook: You are not bad at paperwork. You are doing it twice.
cta: See what one day of jobs looks like in Altair.

beats.narration: Every contractor I talk to says the same thing. The work is fine. It is everything after the work that eats the week.
beats.visualDirection: Fast cuts: hand flipping a worn spiral notebook, a messy whiteboard schedule with crossed-out names, a shoebox overflowing with receipts
beats.caption: The work is fine. It is everything after.

beats.narration: Here is what that actually costs. A tech finishes a job, writes it on paper, and then somebody types it in again tonight.
beats.visualDirection: Working technician in uniform, standing by a service van in a driveway, phone in hand, speaking directly to camera between jobs
beats.caption: Written once. Typed again.

beats.narration: The same unit, the same customer, the second visit — and nobody can find what was done the first time.
beats.visualDirection: Split screen: tech scratching head looking at unfamiliar unit vs. same tech confidently pointing at a part
beats.caption: Second visit. No history.

beats.narration: This is the whole fix. One schedule that everyone is looking at, with the address and the tech already on it.
beats.visualDirection: Screen recording: opening Altair OS to a clean daily schedule view showing jobs with times, addresses, and assigned techs
beats.caption: One schedule. Everyone sees it.

beats.narration: And when the job closes, the invoice is already written. You are not doing the paperwork. The paperwork happened.
beats.visualDirection: Screen recording: technician taps Mark Complete, invoice auto-generates, payment notification pops up on screen
beats.caption: Job closed. Invoice sent.

beats.narration: That is a day a week back. Not from working harder. From stopping doing the same job twice.
beats.visualDirection: Wide shot of a branded HVAC van pulling up to a job site, technician stepping out confidently
beats.caption: A day a week back.
